newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-CANTONA FINED FOR ASSAULTING MAN IN HOTEL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CANTONA FINED FOR ASSAULTING MAN IN HOTEL.

text.p: Eric Cantona, who has fought to repair his image after a kung-fu attack on a fan last year, was ordered on Wednesday to pay damages for assaulting a man in a hotel.

Manchester United striker Cantona, who served 120 hours community service after his attack on a fan during a match at Crystal Palace in January 1995, did not turn up at the hearing before a judge in Liverpool, north-west England.

But lawyers for Tom Doyle said the judge awarded him 350 pounds ($550) damages after he was quizzed about his claim he was grabbed and slapped in the incident at a hotel in Chester in May 1994 where the players had spent a day at the horse races.
Cantona's lawyer, Simon Mather, said the player strongly denied the charge. Mather said Cantona offered 1,000 pounds to settle the claim before the hearing and avoid a "media circus".
"That offer, which was made without any admission of liability whatsoever, was rejected by Mr Doyle, even though it was the maximum that could possibly be awarded.
"In the absence of Eric Cantona the district judge inevitably found in favour of Doyle but awarded him 350 pounds damages and interest of 3.50 pounds," Mather said.
